move2utils: Utility Functions for Movement Data Based on move2

Source: R/move2utils-package.R
move2utils-package.Rd

Utility functions for working with animal movement data stored as 'move2' objects. Four outlier-detection primitives are provided, composable individually or through a unified 'mt_clean_track()' entry-point: (i) a geometric bridge-residual method that scores each fix by its deviation from the time-weighted Brownian-bridge mean of its temporal neighbours, leverage-immune by construction, with an optional directional decomposition for error-morphology classification; (ii) a path-vs-displacement detour ratio that scores each fix by the dimensionless ratio of cumulative path length to chord displacement over a sliding window, time-insensitive and scale-invariant; (iii) a probabilistic method that scores each fix from the empirical joint distribution of speed, angular velocity, and their gap-aware auto-differences, with a non-parametric gap-aware normalisation robust to irregular sampling; (iv) a step-level speed cap with a dip-test-validated data-driven default that catches the boundary transitions of coherent outlier blocks that per-fix detectors structurally cannot resolve. State-aware bridge variants ('mt_flag_outliers_dbgb()', 'mt_flag_outliers_dbbmm()') estimate per-axis bridge motion variance and flag fixes via an envelope rule across three Z channels, useful when behavioural states make a single global threshold over- or under-flag. The package also provides dynamic Brownian bridge movement models (dBBMM) and dynamic bivariate Gaussian bridge (dBGB) variance estimation and utilisation-distribution computation, migrated from the 'move' package C kernels to a modern 'move2'/'sf'/'terra' spatial stack.

Outlier detection

The scientific core is a set of detectors plus a one-call orchestrator. All accept move2 objects in any CRS (longitude/latitude is auto-projected to a local AEQD internally; output is returned in the caller's CRS) and handle single- or multi-track input per individual.

  • mt_clean_track() – one-call entry point: orchestrates the four detectors with an evidence-accumulation decision rule and topological block expansion, iterating to convergence.

  • mt_flag_outliers() – movement-metric probability detector.

  • mt_flag_outliers_bridge() – Brownian-bridge geometric residual.

  • mt_flag_outliers_detour() – path-vs-displacement (time-insensitive).

  • mt_flag_speed_cap() – step-level speed cap; companion mt_suggest_speed_cap().

  • mt_sequential_outliers(), mt_combined_outliers(), mt_peel_speed() – sequential / voting / iterative-peel variants.

  • mt_flag_outliers_dbgb() / mt_flag_outliers_dbbmm() – state-aware bridge detectors (standalone diagnostic).

  • mt_flag_consensus() – turn several detectors' flags into one decision; mt_persistence_score(), mt_diagnose_clean_track(), mt_diagnose_flags() – annotation / post-run diagnostics.

  • v_phys_estimate() – allometric maximum speed from mass + mode.

Utilisation distributions and motion variance

mt_dbbmm_variance() / mt_dbgb_variance() (isotropic / directional dynamic Brownian-bridge variance), mt_dbbmm_ud() / mt_dbgb_ud() (utilisation distributions), mt_motion_variance(), mt_suggest_dbbmm_window(), and the raster utilities ud_volume(), ud_outer_probability(), emd(). These accept any CRS and return the UD in the caller's CRS.

Track utilities

mt_corridor(), mt_thin_time(), mt_thin_distance(), mt_mask_segments(), mt_filter_gps_quality().

Threshold-type vocabulary

The data-driven detectors expose a threshold_type selecting how the flag boundary is found from the data:

  • "gap" – broken-stick gap on the sorted log-scores.

  • "entropy" – density-valley (entropy) cut; safe on clean, unimodal data.

  • "significance" / "percentile" – parametric / quantile cuts (probability detector).

  • "auto" – self-determining cut (detour, speed cap).

  • "fixed" / "hard" – a user-supplied literal threshold / cap.

Consensus vocabulary

mt_flag_consensus() (and mt_clean_track(consensus = )) turn the detectors' flags into a decision. The default is "evidence_corroborated": each detector emits a signed log-likelihood ratio, these are calibrated commensurably into a combined_evidence score, and a fix is flagged when the evidence is positive AND either two detectors corroborate or the high-specificity detour detector is saturated. Other modes: "weighted_evidence" (the smooth evidence score thresholded directly), the Boolean "class_aware" (the prior default), "strict", "majority", "any", "competence_count", and "custom".

Conventions

Functions are prefixed mt_ when they take move2 objects (raster / scalar utilities are not). Preconditions are signalled with stable classed conditions (move2utils_<context>_<reason>); empty or non-finite geometry is rejected rather than silently dropped. See vignette(package = "move2utils") for worked examples.
